headline: Why does my exterior paint peel and crack?
articleBody: It's super frustrating to see your home's exterior paint fail prematurely, right? Usually, peeling or cracking paint isn't just bad luck; it often comes down to prep work, paint quality, or even the weather. If surfaces weren't cleaned properly, or old, loose paint wasn't removed, the new paint just won't stick. Using cheaper paints that lack flexibility or durability can also lead to issues, especially with our Southern California sun and temperature swings. Moisture is another big culprit; if there are leaks behind the walls or poor ventilation, paint will bubble and peel. Painting when it's too hot, too cold, or too humid can mess with the drying process and adhesion. Don't forget about primer – skipping it on certain surfaces or not using the right type can really backfire. To avoid these headaches, make sure you choose a reputable contractor who understands proper surface preparation and uses high-quality materials. A professional eye can spot underlying issues like moisture problems before they become bigger. Ultimately, a good quality job from the start will save you from peeling paint and more expensive fixes down the line. If you're seeing signs of wear, it's a good idea to get an expert opinion.
